title: The Empty Verdict Again
premise: Sable Amberdale, a night-shift dispatcher with a private habit of solving the missing-persons cases that cross his radio, takes on the disappearance of Iris Quill, a reclusive archivist who vanished eleven years ago. When a diary surfaces in which Iris's handwriting continues for years after her disappearance, Sable realizes someone has been impersonating her — or that she never left. Following the diary's coded references to an inherited house and a family trust, he discovers Iris staged her own vanishing to escape a predatory relative, but her plan was hijacked by someone who wanted both the inheritance and her silence. In the end Sable traps the killer by exploiting the one thing they can't fake: Iris's memory of the house itself, closing the case at the cost of the belonging he'd finally begun to feel.
about_author: Felix Voss is the pen name of a former municipal records clerk who spent a decade reading other people's paper trails before writing about them. They live in a rain-heavy port city and claim every good mystery begins in a filing cabinet.

chapters.title: The Frequency of Missing
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. On a slow night shift, dispatcher Sable Amberdale fields a call about a cold case: Iris Quill, missing eleven years, whose sister wants one last look. Sable, known for closing what police can't, accepts. The beat is quiet competence masking loneliness; he takes cases because the dead and lost are easier company than people.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Static
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He visits the Quill house, now half-derelict, and meets the sister, Maren, who hands over a box: photos, a lease, and Iris's diary — which ends abruptly the week she vanished. Sable notices the house was left to Iris in trust, contingent on her being declared dead. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Diary That Kept Writing
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A second diary arrives anonymously at the taxi depot — same handwriting, entries continuing years past the disappearance, describing ordinary days in a house Iris supposedly never returned to. Sable verifies the ink ages match the dates. The beat is vertigo: the file he thought he knew is lying to him.

chapters.title: Handwriting Lessons
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren recalls teaching Iris to write as children and insists no one could forge that hand — then falters, admitting Iris practiced copying their late mother's letters. Doubt creeps in: is Maren protecting a living sister or burying a secret? Beat: love tangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: Night Routes
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cross-referencing taxi logs from the week Iris vanished, Sable finds a fare from the Quill house to a ferry terminal — logged under a driver who later died. Someone left that night, willingly or not. Beat: the first hard evidence, and the thrill of the hunt rekindled.

chapters.title: The Trust Clause
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Digging into probate records, Sable learns the inheritance passes to cousin Aldous Vane if Iris stays missing seven more years. Vane, a charming estate lawyer, invites Sable in, offers help, and quotes details of the case file never made public. Beat: the predator shows its smile.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Searching the sealed upstairs of the Quill house, Sable finds a room kept dusted — bed made, a lamp that still works. Someone has been maintaining it within the last year. Beat: dread turning intimate; the house itself becomes a witness.

chapters.title: Anonymous Fare
chapters.summary: Dispatcher radio POV (second-person plural, the depot's collective ear). A caller books repeated midnight rides to the Quill street but never boards. Sable traces the number to a payphone near the ferry dock. Beat: the invisible presence grows teeth.

chapters.title: Iris's Codes
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The continuation diary's mundane entries hide acrostics naming places: a boathouse, a church registry, a school ledger. Sable realizes Iris — if alive — left a trail only a reader patient as an archivist would find. Beat: reluctant awe; he's falling for a voice on paper.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In a mildewed boathouse, Sable finds supply receipts dated three years ago, signed 'I.Q.' — groceries, batteries, medicine. Either Iris lived hidden nearby until recently, or someone sustained an elaborate fiction. Beat: hope and horror in the same breath.

chapters.title: Vane's Version
chapters.summary: Aldous Vane's POV. Vane privately reviews the case, annoyed that a taxi dispatcher is circling. Flashback reveals he discovered Iris's hiding plan years ago and began intercepting her supplies, keeping her dependent — or replacing her entirely. Beat: chilling control; the reader sees the trap before Sable does.

chapters.title: Maren Breaks
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Confronted with the receipts, Maren confesses she's received unsigned letters from Iris for years and hid them, fearing that proving Iris alive would void the trust and leave them both nothing. Guilt curdles into terror: her silence may have fed the killer. Beat: complicity and grief.

chapters.title: Two Diaries, One Hand
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Forensic comparison shows the continuation diary is genuine Iris — but the final third was written under duress: pressure marks, trembling lines, entries repeating phrases like a hostage script. Iris was alive and captive far longer than anyone guessed. Beat: the mystery sharpens into urgency.

chapters.title: The Ferry Manifest
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. An old ferry worker remembers a woman matching Iris boarding alone years ago — and returning weeks later, thinner, escorted by a man who paid cash. Sable matches the description to Vane's younger associate, now Vane's 'estate manager.' Beat: the net tightens; allies appear where least expected.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Dispatch
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Using the depot's radio codes, Sable sets a trap: he leaks through Vane's clerk that the diaries will be handed to police Friday. If Vane moves to destroy them, he'll lead Sable to wherever Iris — or her body — is kept. Beat: hunter becoming bait; fear worn as armor.

chapters.title: The Empty Room Again
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Checking the maintained bedroom one last time, Sable finds it stripped bare overnight — except a fresh entry torn from the continuation diary, dated tomorrow, describing his own visit in exact detail. Vane knows everything Sable knows. Beat: the watcher watched; isolation closes in.

chapters.title: What Only Iris Knows
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Rereading the childhood letters Maren saved, Sable finds Iris's lifelong private ritual: she always misremembered the house's layout on purpose in writing, a secret game. Any true captive account would contain the error; forged ones wouldn't. Beat: the theme crystallizes — memory as identity, error as signature.

chapters.title: Friday Night Shift
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The handover sting goes wrong: Vane doesn't come for the diaries; instead the depot receives a call in Iris's voice asking Sable, by name, to come alone to the Quill house. It's either rescue or execution. Sable goes. Beat: point of no return, courage over caution.

chapters.title: The House Speaks
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable/Iris POV. Inside, Sable finds Iris alive, weakened, held in the sealed wing for years while Vane siphoned the trust through forged signatures. She confirms the layout errors — proof of authorship and of coercion. Vane arrives. Beat: reunion and confrontation colliding in the dark.

chapters.title: Verdict by Memory
chapters.summary: Sable and Iris POV. Sable springs the real trap: he recites the false layout aloud, and Vane corrects him — citing the true floor plan no outsider could know, implicating himself in the captivity. Iris's recorded testimony plays over the depot radio to arriving police. Beat: climax; the killer undone by knowing too well.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Days
chapters.summary: Iris's POV. Weeks later, Iris testifies, reclaims the house, and burns the coerced pages, keeping only the true ones. She offers Sable the thing he never had: a standing invitation, a place at her table. Beat: grief transmuted into chosen family.

chapters.title: End of Shift
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Back on the night shift, Sable closes Iris's file with the word 'found' and takes a new call — another missing person, another voice in the static. But this time he leaves the depot at dawn and drives to the Quill house for breakfast. Beat: resolution; belonging finally answered.
